title: Checkpoint
description: The small durable progress record enabling resume (work.Checkpoint). Everything else is re-derived from git/forge state.

phase.description: e.g. branch_created, changes_made, pr_opened; prompt_started carries limits (ADR-0114) and briefed carries board (ADR-0124)

commit.description: The commit a reading Run had checked out from the branch under review. Absent when the Run reviewed the base branch.

instructionFiles.description: Agent instruction and configuration files the worker found in the clone before the harness ran (AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at any depth, .cursorrules, .mcp.json, and everything under .claude/, .agents/ and .openhands/), with the SHA-256 of the content it read.

path.description: Slash-separated path relative to the repository root

limits.description: Sent with the prompt_started phase when the agent's prompt starts (ADR-0114): the limits that stop the prompt. promptSeconds counts from promptStartedAt and idleSeconds from the agent's last activity; an absent or zero limit is no limit. ploegd records the first report once and records nothing when promptStartedAt is more than a few minutes before the Run started or after ploegd's clock.

plannedPaths.description: The repository paths the Run plans to change, when it knows them before it pushes (ADR-0123). A path ending in / names a directory. ploegd keeps the newest list per live Shift, at most 100 distinct paths, and names it to other Runs working in the same repository. Optional: absent means unknown, not none.

board.description: Sent once with the briefed phase, after the worker composed the Run's prompt (ADR-0124): the versions only the worker knows (the commit its clone stands on, the graph commits it read the knowledge at), the keys of the Work Item Notes and the paths of the concepts the briefing showed, and each section's budget and use. ploegd records the first report on the Run; a value outside its bounds is left out.

items.description: One section of a Run's briefing (ADR-0124): its fixed budget in bytes, what it used, how many items it showed and left out, and a digest of its text.
